fluff.overview:
The Silverback Coastal Cutter is a Lyran Alliance field modification of the ancient Silverfin, introduced in 3058 as a dedicated electronic warfare escort for high-value wet navy assets. Blue water navies in the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces developed the conversion informally, stripping the torpedo launchers in favor of a Guardian ECM Suite and additional machine guns. The resulting vessel proved immediately popular among planetary militia navies looking to extend their limited capital-ship complements with electronic protection rather than direct firepower.

Where the Silverfin is a patrol tool of broad applicability, the Silverback fills a narrower and more specific role: keeping enemy targeting solutions away from Lyran naval flagships. Its recognition in LAAF wet navy records formalized what had begun as a local adaptation, and the design spread quickly through Alliance coastal forces.
fluff.capabilities:
The Silverback retains the Silverfin's 40-ton hydrofoil hull, 17-ton ICE powerplant, and Windancer Lightwave armor unchanged. Flank speed remains 120 km/h and the polymer composite foils carry over without modification. Fuel capacity increases by half a ton over the base Silverfin, extending operational range to approximately 2,352 km.

Armament shifts from the Silverfin's torpedo-machine gun combination to three machine guns in the forward turret, all guided by an Advanced Fire Control system. The elimination of the torpedo launchers was a deliberate trade, freeing tonnage for the Silverback's defining upgrade: a Guardian ECM Suite weighing 1.5 tons. The Guardian system disrupts enemy targeting and guidance systems across a meaningful area, making the Silverback particularly valuable when stationed alongside slower, better-armed flagships.

The armor protection remains identical to the base Silverfin (one ton of BAR 7 Windancer Lightwave commercial plating) meaning the Silverback is no more survivable in direct combat than the vessel it was built from. It must rely on its ECM disruption and hydrofoil speed to avoid being hit. The HUNTER communications electronics are likewise inherited unchanged and retain the same fifty-year overhaul requirement.
fluff.deployment:
The Silverback serves exclusively within Lyran Alliance wet navy forces, deployed as an electronic warfare screen for high-value naval vessels such as Jormungand-class cruisers. Typical doctrine pairs multiple Silverbacks in close escort of a flagship, providing overlapping ECM coverage to deny enemy guided-weapon solutions. The design is unsuited to independent patrol or sustained combat and depends on proximity to better-armored assets for operational effectiveness.

The Blue Hole Navy maintains a standing complement of at least three Silverbacks on permanent assignment to the BHS Brynhild, an arrangement widely cited within Alliance naval commands as a cost-effective approach to flagship protection. Other Lyran planetary militia navies have replicated this pattern to varying degrees depending on local resources and the perceived threat environment.
fluff.history:
The Silverback emerged not from a formal development program but from ad hoc modifications carried out by Lyran Alliance coastal naval technicians in the years following the Clan Invasion. The appearance of Clan naval assets and improved guided-weapon systems made electronic warfare protection increasingly critical for Lyran surface fleets, whose aging capital ships could not easily absorb direct hits from advanced munitions. Technicians found that the Silverfin's cargo and torpedo space was sufficient to house a Guardian ECM Suite with room left for additional machine guns, and the hydrofoil hull's proven reliability made the modification straightforward to execute in field conditions.

The conversion proved popular enough to earn formal LAAF recognition by 3058, and the designation Silverback was entered into Lyran Alliance wet navy rolls as a distinct variant. Planetary militia navies throughout the Alliance quickly adopted the pattern, as it offered a way to extend the protective umbrella of limited capital ship complements without requiring new construction. Critical acclaim for the design spread through Lyran naval circles following the Blue Hole Navy's deployment of three Silverbacks as a permanent escort force for the BHS Brynhild, the planet's sole Jormungand-class cruiser. The Blue Hole arrangement became an informal model referenced by other planetary commands seeking to protect high-value vessels with minimal resources.
